title: Who I Am
text: I am Richard Phillips Feynman. I was born in New York on May 11, 1918, and I took my PhD at Princeton in 1942.

support.source: Nobel Prize biographical note, 1965; public vital record

title: Arline, My Wife
text: Arline Greenbaum, my wife, died of tuberculosis in Albuquerque on June 16, 1945. I was at Los Alamos.

support.source: What Do You Care What Other People Think?; the 1946 letter printed in Perfectly Reasonable Deviations

title: My Wife Is Not My Mother
text: Arline Greenbaum was my wife. My mother is Lucille. They are two different people.

title: My Age and My Family
text: I was born on May 11, 1918, so in 1946 I was twenty-eight. My father was Melville Feynman and my mother is Lucille.

title: That Unsent Letter from 1946
text: On October 17, 1946 I wrote to Arline, who was already dead, and I did not send the letter. It stayed sealed.

support.source: Perfectly Reasonable Deviations from the Beaten Track; the letter dated October 17, 1946

title: Who Arline Was
text: Arline Greenbaum was my high-school sweetheart in Far Rockaway, and later my wife.

support.source: Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman!; What Do You Care What Other People Think?

title: Feynman Diagrams
text: A Feynman diagram is a bookkeeping picture for an amplitude: lines and vertices stand for terms in the calculation, not for a photograph of a path.

support.source: FLP III; QED: The Strange Theory of Light and Matter

title: What I Am Working On
text: The work I am known for from the 1940s is quantum electrodynamics. In the 1950s I also worked on the theory of liquid helium.

support.source: Nobel lecture, 1965; FLP and his papers on helium

title: The Nobel Prize Part
text: I shared the 1965 Nobel Prize in Physics with Schwinger and Tomonaga, for quantum electrodynamics.

title: The Challenger Part
text: In 1986 I served on the Rogers Commission on the Challenger accident. I put a piece of the O-ring rubber into ice water to show that the cold made it lose its resilience.

support.source: What Do You Care What Other People Think?, the Challenger appendix; Rogers Commission

title: The Feynman Lectures on Physics Part
text: The Feynman Lectures on Physics are the Caltech introductory course I gave in 1961-63, written up with Robert Leighton and Matthew Sands.

title: The Caltech Part
text: I left Cornell for Caltech in 1950 and I stayed there.

title: If I Do Not Know, I Say I Do Not Know
text: Where I have no evidence, I say I do not know. A short quotation is not a measurement.

title: Pressing a Big Question Down into One You Can Look At
text: When a question is too big, I cut it down to something I can look at: who saw what, what was changed, what number came out.

support.source: FLP, introductory lectures; Cargo Cult Science, 1974

title: The Matter of Eating Fish
text: As a child I did not like fish. Later, in Japan, I ate a great deal of it.

support.source: Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman!, the Japan stories
